youtube.title: Which animal has the strongest bite? Scientists measured it 🦷
youtube.description:
The river giant with the famous yawn, the big cat, or the third one? Scientists put a meter between the jaws of each and one of them came out at more than three times the big cat's force — the strongest bite ever measured on a living animal. The strange part: the same jaws can be held shut with a rubber band.
Which did you pick?

research.topic: Strongest measured bite of any living animal: the saltwater crocodile (Crocodylus porosus). Erickson et al. (PLoS ONE, 2012) recorded 16,460 newtons (about 3,700 psi) from a 5.2 m saltwater crocodile, the highest bite force ever directly measured on a living animal. Lions measure roughly 4,000–4,500 N (about 650–1,000 psi); hippos are estimated at about 8,100 N (about 1,800 psi). Crocodilian jaw muscles are massive for closing but weak for opening, so the mouth can be held shut by hand or with tape or a band. Saltwater crocodiles live in rivers, estuaries and coasts from eastern India to northern Australia; the largest males exceed 6 m and ambush prey at the water's edge.

myths.myth: The hippo, with the biggest gape in Africa, has the strongest bite.
myths.reality: A hippo's bite is estimated at about half the saltwater crocodile's measured force; the crocodile holds the record for a living animal.
